ai.title: Sequential file processing per path
ai.summary: Refactored `main-prompt.ts` to process file blocks sequentially per path, preventing race conditions from concurrent writes to the same file. Updated `process-file-block.ts` to accept an initial content promise and return full content alongside patches, normalizing line endings before patch generation. Internal backend change affecting `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/process-file-block.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant edits the same file more than once in a single response, it now waits for each edit to finish before starting the next one instead of trying to do them all at the same time. This prevents the edits from colliding and overwriting each other, which could lose your content or produce a broken file. You won't see a button or setting for this; it just makes the assistant's file writing more reliable behind the scenes.

ai.title: Normalize line endings in processFileBlock
ai.summary: Added `patch.replaceAll('\n', lineEnding)` in `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` to normalize line endings within the patch string. This ensures consistent line ending usage when processing file blocks. Scope limited to backend file processing logic.

eli5.text: When the backend processes a file block, it now normalizes line endings within the patch string by replacing all instances of one line-break character with the standard line ending used in the system. This affects the internal file-processing pipeline and ensures consistency when handling files that may have been created on different operating systems. If you looked at the processed output, you'd notice that line breaks are now uniform throughout, rather than potentially mixing different line-ending styles in a single file block.

ai.title: Update CLI prompt on directory change
ai.summary: Added `this.setPrompt()` call in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to refresh the prompt after directory changes. This ensures the displayed working directory updates correctly when navigating via `cd`.

eli5.text: When you navigated between folders during a session, your session now correctly shows the new folder path right away instead of displaying the old one. Previously, the address shown in your prompt stayed stuck on the folder you started in until you manually refreshed, so it could look like you were still in the old folder even though you'd moved. This only affects interactive sessions where you manually change directories; it does not change how scripts or automated commands behave. This is live today.

ai.title: Bump codebuff version to 1.0.182
ai.summary: Version bump in `npm-app/package.json` from 1.0.181 to 1.0.182. Internal release preparation.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant, updating to this version prevents a crash that happened when undoing a command or finishing a response while the assistant was unable to save progress normally; it now handles the missing-progress case instead of breaking. The same update also adds a quiet background logging tool that helps the team spot problems without you seeing extra output, and it keeps the assistant from saving duplicate progress files for commands that already manage their own history. These changes take effect the moment you run the newer version of the assistant.

ai.title: Suppress git command output in checkpoints
ai.summary: Added `stdio: 'ignore'` to `execFileSync` calls in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts`. This prevents git status and progress messages from polluting the agent's output stream during checkpoint creation. The change affects `gitCommandIsAvailable`, `getLatestCommit`, `gitAddAll`, and `gitCommit`.

eli5.text: The assistant creates checkpoints by saving your work progress to a hidden folder, and it uses git in the background to do that. Previously, git kept printing status messages and progress text into the output you see while the checkpoint was being saved, cluttering the results with technical noise. Now, the assistant silences all of those internal git messages so only the checkpoint-saving action itself is visible. If you looked at the checkpoint process today, you would see a cleaner result without the extra git lines mixed in.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.183
ai.summary: Bump npm package version from 1.0.182 to 1.0.183 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant from an npm install, your next install will pull version 1.0.183, which silently hides git command output when saving checkpoints and now processes files one at a time in order instead of all jumbled up, so you won't see noisy git progress messages cluttering your terminal and file operations will happen in a steadier sequence. Behind the scenes it's just a routine version-label bump that packages these small internal improvements together; the change is live today for anyone who installs this version.

ai.title: Expand createplan tool triggers for new features and refactoring
ai.summary: The `create_plan` tool description now explicitly includes "new feature" and "refactoring" as triggers alongside the existing "plan" keyword. The system prompt separates complex request handling into distinct directives: `think_deeply` for complexity and `create_plan` for feature/refactoring starts. This change applies to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/tools.ts`. The previous combined condition for `think_deeply` was simplified to focus solely on complexity.

eli5.text: The assistant now prepares a plan whenever you ask it to build a new feature or reorganize existing code, not just when you tell it to plan. You'll notice it offers to sketch out steps before diving in, whether you're adding something new or reshaping something already there. This guidance lives in the behind-the-scenes instructions that steer how the assistant decides which tools to reach for.

ai.title: Add blacklisted terminal commands
ai.summary: Added blacklist check for 'halt', 'reboot', 'yes' in checkTerminalCommand. Blocks these commands before LLM validation. Internal security guard.

eli5.text: The assistant now silently refuses to run three specific terminal commands, ‘halt’, ’reboot’, and ‘yes’, before it even checks them against its safety rules, blocking them outright as a guardrail. If you were watching the backend process internal commands, those three would disappear from the queue immediately instead of being passed through to the normal validation step. This is an internal security measure already in place and does not change what you can currently do.

ai.title: Feed endpoint switches to Substack JSON API
ai.summary: web/src/app/api/feed/route.ts now fetches https://news.codebuff.com/api/v1/posts instead of the RSS feed. Zod schemas validate the JSON response, replacing fragile XML regex parsing. This internal change affects only the Web feed route. The Article interface remains unchanged, mapping Substack fields to existing properties.

eli5.text: The internal news feed that powers the articles on the site now pulls content from CodeBuff's own JSON data source instead of parsing raw XML text. You won't see a difference while browsing, but internally this swap replaces error-prone text-pattern matching with structured validation, so future feed items are matched against expected formats before display. This is active today for the site's internal feed system only.

ai.title: Show usage credits on each message
ai.summary: New `message-cost-response` action pushes real-time credit usage to clients after each LLM message. `saveMessage` in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts` locates the active WebSocket via `SWITCHBOARD` and sends the cost immediately. Auth logic moved from `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts` to shared `backend/src/util/check-auth.ts`, enabling a new `POST /api/usage` endpoint in `backend/src/api/usage.ts`. `genUsageResponse` signature changed to accept `clientSessionId` and `requestedByUser` flags.

eli5.text: After the assistant sends you a message, you'll now see how many of your usage credits that message cost, shown to you right away. This works through your active connection to the service, which pushes the cost information to you immediately after each response. The change also adds a new endpoint for checking your usage and moves authentication handling so that credit tracking works consistently across both real-time connections and regular API requests.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.184
ai.summary: Package version in npm-app/package.json incremented from 1.0.183 to 1.0.184. Internal release marker for the codebuff package. No functional changes or API modifications included.

eli5.text: The assistant's planning tool now recognizes requests for new features and code reorganization without needing the exact word "plan" to start. When you ask it to plan something, it will also flag potentially dangerous terminal commands like halt, reboot, or yes before running anything. The assistant can also show you how many usage credits each message costs in real time, and its feed content pulls from a different source for better updates.

ai.title: Version bump 1.0.185
ai.summary: Bumped npm-app package version to 1.0.185. Updates `npm-app/package.json` for release metadata. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: A routine version-label update was published that increments the package number used by install tools, so the package manager sees a fresh, current build. No visible features or behaviors changed for users; this keeps automated installs from pulling a stale copy. The version number advances, but the assistant's capabilities stay the same.

ai.title: Version 1.0.186
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.186. Updates `npm-app/package.json`.

eli5.text: The assistant's packaging was bumped to a new release label, which is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that keeps installations current. This release bundle also includes sequential file processing per path, normalized line endings during processing, a refreshed CLI prompt on directory change, the codebuff tool advancing to its own new label, and quieter git command output during checkpoints. If you simply update to this version, you won't notice any direct change in how the assistant behaves; it just stays installable and aligned with the latest labeled bundle.

ai.title: Release 1.0.187 and remove pino logger
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.187 in `npm-app/package.json`. Removed `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts`, deleting the `pino`-based debug logging implementation. This cleanup removes the `withLoggerContext` helper and file transport configuration from the CLI package.

eli5.text: The assistant stopped writing debug notes to a log file as it runs. Behind the scenes, the team removed the logging tool and bumped the version number. The tool you interact with looks and works the same today; you just won't see any debug tracing being saved anymore.

ai.title: Version 1.0.188
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.188. `npm-app/src/client.ts` replaces `logger.error` with `console.error` for init action failures. `npm-app/package.json` updates version metadata.

eli5.text: The assistant now records startup errors using the browser or system's built-in error log instead of a custom internal logger, so any failure messages shown during launch come from the standard place you'd normally check for app problems. If you watch the screen while it boots and something goes wrong, the error text will look slightly different but still be readable. This is a small behind-the-scenes tweak that just landed today and does not change how the tool works day to day.

ai.title: Add redo command and checkpoint parent tracking
ai.summary: Implements redo functionality and parent tracking in CheckpointManager. Adds `redo` CLI command, `parentId` field to Checkpoint interface, and `restoreUndoCheckpoint`/`restoreRedoCheckpoint` methods. Worker responses now include original message for validation.

eli5.text: You can now reverse an undo. When you told the assistant to undo a step, the previous state was lost for good; now a new redo command brings the assistant back to the version that was active just before you undid it. Behind the scenes, each saved point now remembers which point came before it, so the system can walk forward and backward through your recent edits instead of only backward. The change is live today for anyone using the assistant in the terminal, but it only covers the most recent undo-redo pair, not the full history.

ai.title: Hide prompt when rejecting empty input
ai.summary: CLI clears readline prompt before validating empty input in `handleUserInput`. Prevents prompt display when input is rejected. Affects `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you press Enter without typing anything, the assistant now waits cleanly instead of flashing a leftover prompt on the screen. It clears the old prompt before deciding the input is empty, so the next prompt only appears when it's actually asking for input. If you ever left the line blank, you'll no longer see a stray prompt flicker before the assistant moved on.

ai.title: Fix git fallback logic in checkpoints file manager
ai.summary: Corrected git command execution in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts` to prevent unnecessary fallback to isomorphic-git when native git succeeds. Adjusted `stdio` configuration for `git status` and ensured `gitCommit` returns valid commit hashes from both native and fallback paths. This internal fix improves checkpoint reliability by properly handling git command outputs and return values.

eli5.text: When you save your work, the system checks whether there are unsaved changes by running a git command. Previously, even when this git command succeeded and found changes, the system would incorrectly ignore the result and fall back to a slower alternative method, causing inconsistent checkpoint behavior. Now the system properly trusts the successful git output and only uses the slower fallback when git actually fails, making your checkpoint saves more reliable.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.189
ai.summary: Version incremented to 1.0.189 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release bump for codebuff package. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The AI dev assistant you use has quietly rolled out a small update to its latest build today, and nothing about how it works for you has visibly changed. Behind the scenes, the team packaged together a few recent improvements into this new version, including the ability to undo and redo actions in the assistant’s memory system and a small tweak that stops stray text from flashing on the screen when you submit an empty command. If you’re running the assistant today, you’ll automatically benefit from these refinements the next time you start a session.

ai.title: Remove debug log from CheckpointManager
ai.summary: Deleted a stray console.log('asdf', {targetId}) in npm-app/src/checkpoints/checkpoint-manager.ts. This cleanup removes unnecessary debug noise from checkpoint restoration logic. Scope limited to the checkpoint-manager.ts file within npm-app.

eli5.text: The checkpoint restoration feature used to print a stray test message ('asdf') along with some internal data every time it ran. That debug spam is now gone, so when the system restores a saved state, it does so quietly without leaving behind any leftover test output.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.190
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.190 in `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The current build rolled out under a new release number (1.0.190). Updating to it mainly cleans up behind the scenes by removing a leftover debug message that was printing during checkpoint operations. You wouldn't notice any speed or feature difference; it's the same assistant, just tidy internal logging.

ai.title: Remove redundant spinner start in client.ts
ai.summary: Removed Spinner.get().start() call in npm-app/src/client.ts during incomplete prompt continuation. Eliminates redundant UI spinner activation when sending tool results via WebSocket. Internal cleanup only.

eli5.text: When the assistant was still thinking through a multi-step task and sent partial results back, it used to show the spinning loading icon a second time on top of the one already visible. The spinning icon now starts only once per action, so you won't see a second spinner flicker on while a tool result is on its way. This smooths out the small visual twitch and is purely internal cleanup with no new features.

ai.title: Stop spinner before tool calls in client
ai.summary: Added `Spinner.get().stop()` before state assignment in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. Prevents spinner from running during tool execution. Internal client behavior change.

eli5.text: When you run a command, the tool now stops showing its spinning progress indicator before it actually starts the work. You would see the spinner disappear right before the task begins, instead of it continuing to spin while the work runs. This affects anyone using the command-line tool and makes the timing of when the spinner is visible more consistent.
